root_idea.summary: The root centers on the spear or lance as an instrument of thrusting and piercing.
root_idea.development: From the spear's thrusting action, the lexical field extends to kicking, reciprocal spear-combat, pointed or horned things, and figurative expressions based on spear imagery.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular dictionary citation form رُمْح; the Quran occurrence itself is the plural رِمَاح.

senses.definition: Spear or lance: a weapon used for thrusting or piercing.
senses.usage_conditions: The attested Quran form is the possessive plural رِمَاحُكُمْ, “your spears,” referring to the weapon rather than to a generic projectile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To thrust or pierce someone with a spear or lance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the object is the person struck by the spear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kick or strike with the hind leg or legs; of a locust, to strike pebbles with the hind leg or legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly said of a horse, ass, mule, or other solid-hoofed animal; the usage is also extended to camels and she-camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gallop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Marked as vulgar modern usage in the cited lexicographic evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of lightning, to gleam or flash in slight, closely spaced flashes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage applied specifically to lightning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with someone in thrusting or piercing with a spear or lance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III reciprocal or mutual-combat construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with one another in thrusting or piercing with spears or lances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI reciprocal construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figurative spear-based expressions: for enmity or trouble to arise between people; a long and distressing day; people united against someone as one man; and a person looking intensely in fear or anger as though his eyes were on two spears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional idiomatic or figurative applications of the spear image, not additional literal weapon senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper name or euphemistic designation for the penis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of the diminutive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A unit of angular or linear measure called a spear-length or spear measure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in astronomical usage and in some legal works; the reported size is not uniform across sources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the buhmā grass and similar pasture, to put forth prickles or become dry and prickly, thereby resisting grazing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression describing the grass as acquiring spears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to become fat or yield milk plentifully, so that their owner is deterred from slaughtering them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression also used in descriptions such as نَاقَةٌ ذَاتُ رُمْحٍ and إِبِلٌ ذَوَاتُ رِمَاحٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The plague or pestilence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stings of scorpions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression likening the scorpion's stings to spears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A term for a long-legged species of jerboa; its tail is called رُمَيْح.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited passage is textually corrupted in places, so the exact expression and details of the identification remain uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vice of kicking or striking with the hind leg, especially in a solid-hoofed animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized form describing a defect for which a sold animal could be returned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse, camel, or other beast habitually given to kicking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of an animal with a kicking disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The craft or art of making spears or lances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun naming the occupation or skill.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker of spears or lances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun; it may describe a skilled spear-maker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bow, forcefully propelling an arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used attributively of a bow; the forceful propulsion is expressed without requiring an overt object in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thrust or piercing with a spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reported explanation of a poetic use and is explicitly left unresolved in the evidence; it may instead be an ungoverned verbal noun related to رَمَحَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poverty, need, or want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative meaning attributed to this derived form; it is not the meaning of the weapon noun رُمْح.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who thrusts or pierces another with a spear or lance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who has or carries a spear or lance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive adjective of the pattern used for someone characterized by possessing the named object, rather than an agent noun derived from a verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Arcturus, a star named “the spear-bearing Simāk.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional astronomical proper name; the spear image refers to the star preceding it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horned bull, especially a wild bull.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative or descriptive usage based on the bull's pair of horns.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Kicking or striking with the hind legs.
Locust striking pebbles with its hind leg.
Literal spear noun, spear-based idioms, and the diminutive figurative designation.
Jerboa and tail terminology, retained with a textual-corruption caution.
Plural of the spear noun, covered by the Quranic weapon sense.
Forceful bow usage and an explicitly uncertain poetic spear-thrust interpretation.
Figurative meaning of poverty or need.
Possessive adjective meaning one who has a spear.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence is the plural رِمَاح in 5:94; the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form رُمْح.
The derived, idiomatic, technical, and figurative branches listed under broader Classical Arabic meanings are not additional Quranic occurrences.
The poetic explanation of رَمَّاحَة as a spear-thrust is unresolved in the supplied evidence, and the jerboa passage involving رُمَيْح is textually corrupt.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The poetic use of رَمَّاحَة is variously analyzed as a spear-thrust or as a verbal noun related to رَمَحَ; it is retained as a qualified Classical meaning rather than treated as certain.
The expression and analysis in the Lane passage for ذُو رُمَيْح are partly corrupted or incomplete, so its jerboa and tail identification is reported cautiously.
